summary: CDAS proposes a weaker, distribution-matching (JSD) objective with distributed interchange interventions for bi-directional LLM steering, framed as a more faithful alternative to Lang./PO objectives. The paper is thoughtfully positioned and unusually honest about mixed AXBENCH results, with the strongest evidence in utility-preserving concept-suppression case studies (refusal override up to 70B; CoT backdoor neutralization). It is a credible borderline ICLR contribution, but novelty is partly compositional, primary-benchmark wins are layer-/scale-contingent, and statistical/ablation support is thinner than the acceptance bar typically demands.
strengths: Clear motivation contrasting strong token/preference supervision with full-vocabulary distribution matching, plus an explicit link to DII/DAS-style intervention protocols for bi-directional control.

Evaluation spans a standard steering benchmark (AXBENCH with fair factor selection) and two nontrivial safety case studies that measure both control success and utility/distributional faithfulness (benchmarks + KL).

Calibration is comparatively strong: the paper reports unit- vs tuned-factor gaps, layer sensitivity, RePS overfitting signals, and a limitations section that scopes when CDAS is preferable rather than claiming uniform SOTA.

key_concerns.issue: Core thesis that natural DII-sampled factors yield faithful, more tuning-free steering is undercut by large unit-vs-tuned gaps on AXBENCH, where CDAS often trails RePS/Lang except at selected larger-model layers.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a deeper analysis of when/why unit factors fail (concept strength, layer, model scale), and either improve the training-time factor distribution or demonstrate a clearly superior tuning-free protocol vs RePS under matched budgets.

key_concerns.issue: Component isolation is incomplete: DAS (Lang.+DII) partially ablates the objective, but there is little systematic ablation of JSD vs KL/other divergences, DII vs addition/clamping under the same loss, or one-to-many source-token choices beyond grid search.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact ablation matrix isolating objective, intervention operator, and source-token policy on at least one AXBENCH setting and one case study.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is uneven: AXBENCH fair averages and backdoor 3-seed SE exist, but many headline comparisons lack uncertainty, significance tests, or multi-seed training variance for CDAS vs RePS/Lang.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report multi-seed means±SE (or bootstrap CIs) for primary tables and pairwise significance for key claims (e.g., 9B L20 win; refusal suppression on 8B/70B; backdoor ASR).

key_concerns.issue: Breadth is limited relative to generality language: AXBENCH is Gemma-2 only; interventions remain rank-1; backdoor utility uses tinyBenchmarks of 100 examples.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add one non-Gemma family on CONCEPT500 (or a subset) and/or strengthen utility evaluation with fuller benchmarks where feasible.

key_concerns.issue: Occasional tension between ‘causally grounded / faithful concept features’ rhetoric and the explicit remark that CDAS is not causal variable localization.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Tighten abstract/intro wording to ‘DAS-inspired distributional steering’ and reserve causal claims for what the interventions empirically demonstrate.

questions_for_authors: Under matched inference-time factor-search budgets, does CDAS still outperform RePS on Gemma-2-9B L20, or is the reported edge partly an artifact of different factor-selection protocols?
Why does replacing the CDAS objective with Lang. (your DAS baseline) collapse refusal-suppression performance below DIM—does this indicate objective–protocol mismatch or optimization instability?
How sensitive are results to the gpt-4o-mini–augmented contrastive pairs and to the chosen <model> source token; would human-written neutrals or multi-token DII change rankings?
Can you quantify ‘overfitting’ for RePS beyond qualitative notes (e.g., train vs held-out suppression gap, or distributional KL vs CDAS) in a single comparable table?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly appropriately scoped in the conclusion (complementary; scale-/utility-dependent), but earlier ‘faithful/causally grounded pathway’ language slightly outruns the evidence given mixed primary-benchmark results and necessary factor tuning.

significance.justification: Utility-preserving bi-directional steering and safety case studies are relevant to the LLM control community, but mixed AXBENCH wins limit immediate practice-changing impact.

novelty.justification: JSD full-vocabulary matching plus DII for steering is a coherent new combination, yet ingredients (DAS/DII, distribution matching, steering vectors) are largely known and the advance feels compositional.

rigor.justification: Method and controls are generally sound and baselines are competitive, but incomplete objective/protocol ablations and protocol asymmetries (unit vs tuned factors) weaken some causal attributions.

statistical_soundness.justification: Fair splits and limited seed/SE reporting help, yet primary tables often lack multi-seed variance and formal significance for the headline comparisons.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper openly reports underperformance vs RePS/Lang in places, unit-factor failures, layer sensitivity, and clear limitations rather than overselling uniform SOTA.

clarity.justification: Structure and problem setup are clear and the objective is specified carefully, though dense method prose and naming (CDAS vs DAS baseline) can confuse.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR organization (intro, related work, method, benchmark, case studies, conclusion/limitations) is complete and appropriately scoped in length.

reproducibility.justification: Data construction, intervention forms, layer choices, factor rules, and metrics are described in enough detail to reproduce in principle once anonymized artifacts are restored.

related_work.justification: Steering objectives, DAS/causal localization, distribution matching, and safety probes are positioned fairly with a clear delineation of contribution versus Lang./PO/DIM.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative comparisons (AXBENCH scores, refusal/suppression, utility/KL, ASR curves with SE) that directly support the paper’s claims rather than decorate them.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence spans concepts and two safety settings up to 70B, but Gemma-only AXBENCH, rank-1 only, and tiny utility sets under-support broad generality claims.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: useful, well-calibrated steering method with solid case studies, but needs tighter ablations/statistics and a clearer primary win condition to be a clear accept.
